selector.champion: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
selector.rationale: Patient has a history of NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (<25%) and presented with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which is consistent with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The presence of sinus tachycardia, global hypokinesis, and increased QRS voltages in precordial leads also support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: While the patient has a history of hypertension, the current presentation is more consistent with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
rejected.why: Although the ECG findings suggest Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, the patient's overall clinical presentation is more consistent with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
